strings.name: Ingrid Daubechies
strings.summary: Daubechies moved from theoretical physics to applied mathematics, constructing compactly supported orthogonal wavelets for signal processing and image compression. She worked at Bell Labs, Princeton and Duke and applied mathematics to art analysis. The first woman to lead the IMU (2011–2014), she supports mathematics education and women’s participation and won the 2023 Wolf Prize.
strings.influence.rationale: Advances wavelet theory and applications, influencing signal processing, image compression and applied mathematics education.
strings.facts.f2.value: Vrije Universiteit Brussel: physics bachelor’s (1975), theoretical physics PhD (1980).
strings.highlights.h1.title: Compactly supported wavelets
strings.highlights.h1.text: Linked abstract theory with finite computation for digital signal processing.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Education and mathematical institutions
strings.highlights.h2.text: Led the IMU and supported women entering mathematical research.
strings.timeline.t1.title: ESI Medal announced
strings.timeline.t1.text: Institute announced its 2026 medal; the ceremony was postponed to 2027.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Wolf Prize
strings.timeline.t2.text: Awarded the mathematics prize for wavelet theory and modern time-frequency analysis.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Duke and IMU leadership
strings.timeline.t3.text: Joined Duke and began her 2011–2014 IMU presidency.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Princeton professorship
strings.timeline.t4.text: Became Princeton’s first woman full professor of mathematics.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Wavelet paper
strings.timeline.t5.text: Published her landmark study of compactly supported orthonormal wavelet bases.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joined Bell Labs
strings.timeline.t6.text: Joined Bell Labs in the US, connecting mathematical theory and applications.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Physics doctorate
strings.timeline.t7.text: Completed a theoretical physics doctorate in Brussels and continued mathematical research.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Born in Houthalen
strings.timeline.t8.text: Born in Belgium; later studied physics in Brussels.
